prompt: A Helm render succeeds, but the API rejects one Deployment and no new Pod appears. Diagnose the first failed boundary and define the safe repair path.
directAnswer: Bind cluster, namespace, release identity, source commit, chart/dependency and renderer versions, ordered values and render digest. A successful client render proves only template evaluation. Capture the server dry-run or API error, including API group/version/kind/name, field path, admission policy and audit ID. Classify schema/discovery, authorization, admission or immutable-field rejection. Repair the smallest source input/template or planned migration; do not bypass admission or repeatedly upgrade. Re-render deterministically, repeat schema/policy/server validation, review the normalized diff, perform one bounded release, observe generation/conditions, then verify the user operation.
foundation: Client rendering and API acceptance are different gates.
reasoningSteps: Classify schema, authorization, admission or immutable field.
seniorAnswer: I do not treat more templating as a server fix. I preserve the exact proposal and API decision, correct the source at the earliest failed boundary, then prove the entire chain through the user operation.
weakAnswer: Run helm upgrade again with force.
whyWeak: Force or retry can replace resources, repeat hooks and enlarge impact without correcting the rejection.

followUps.answer: It binds later validation and incident evidence to the exact proposed bytes.
Replacement can change identity, availability and data/resource lifecycle; it is not a generic retry flag.
Service endpoints, dependencies and the original user-level operation or SLI.
